@ an up that widens the window of a down: the output of a part dealt by a down 2 and read by an up 4 is not lost by the next down 4
@ the bundle of an up that a down 2 deals is read by the caller in the frame it was made, and the same through a down 4 and an up 4
@ a down then an up over an output at sample * N: the array that the down deals is read by the runs of the up in the frame of the run, with no delay
@ sample_rate() is divided by the down and multiplied by the up, from the outermost modifier in
@ the time of a part in an up is N times the number of the part outside it plus the run (S-1217)
@ the time of a part in an up that a bundle is read from is the same for chains that cancel to the same ratio
@ a slow stage of the head runs at the runs of the up whose counter is a multiple of its ratio: only j = 0 for sample / 2 under up 2
@ only the outer down gathers: an input at sample / 2 through a down 2, an up 4 and a down 4 is the stream 4 frames late, each element held 2 frames
@ an up that cuts the bundle of an input into its runs: x[0] .. x[3] of the 4 elements go 2 and 2 to the runs
@ a value of an up read as a bundle: the runs are in order, and the parameter is the one of the frame
@ an up in par~ and in if~: each copy has its own runs, the arm that is not taken runs too
@ the delays of the boundaries add in a chain of depth 3: 4 samples for two of up 2 down 2, none for two of down 2 up 2
@ an output with no Default through a down and an up needs none: it is made by the stage that runs it
- the calls of process cut the run anywhere, a call of 0 frames too: the same values for chains with an up (§13.4)
@ eight calls of one frame give the same
@ reset after any number of frames: the runs, the rings, the arrays and the time are those of a state just made (S-1186)
